title: Private Deploy Data Escrow and Business Continuity Specification
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview
--------
This document defines Redwood Inference's baseline specification for data escrow and business continuity (BCP) requirements for Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Security, and Field Operations teams who negotiate, onboard, and operate customer Private deployments. The goal is to ensure customers and Redwood have an auditable, testable, and legally defensible plan to preserve service continuity and evidence in regulated or high-risk scenarios.

Scope and applicability
----------------------
- Applies to all Private deployments where customer or contract terms require escrowed copies of: model artifacts, runtime images, KV-cache snapshots, tenant metadata, and telemetry evidence bundles.
- Covers both online (cloud VPC) and air-gapped on-prem installations.
- Does NOT replace customer-managed backups; this spec defines Redwood-managed escrow for contractually required evidence, handoff, and emergency transfer.

Key definitions
---------------
- Escrow Package: A bundled, signed archive that contains artifacts listed in the "Escrow package contents" section.
- Evidence Bundle: Time-sliced telemetry and audit logs required for incident forensics and regulatory audits.
- Escrow Agent: Third-party or internal legal custodian responsible for holding escrow packages under contract.
- Activation Event: Predefined incidents that trigger release or transfer of escrowed materials (e.g., vendor bankruptcy, contractual termination, or prolonged inability to provide service).

Business continuity targets
---------------------------
- Recovery Point Objective (RPO): Default 24 hours for model artifacts and runtime images; configurable to 1 hour for customers with critical RPOs (documented in the order form).
- Recovery Time Objective (RTO): Default 48 hours from activation to verified handover; expedited 8–24 hours for customers with a verified expedited clause.
- Evidence preservation SLA: Telegraphing and sealing of an evidence bundle within 2 hours of an incident detection (operational detection by Redwood or customer).

Escrow provider and custody model
---------------------------------
1. Preferred model: Use a neutral third-party escrow agent with experience in software and cryptographic key custody. Recommended vendors: IronCladEscrow (example), LegalVault, or similar (procurement should validate).
2. Alternate model: Redwood acts as steward with dual-control escrow (Redwood + customer legal representative) for customers who disallow third-party escrow. This requires additional indemnities and legal review.

Escrow package contents (minimum)
----------------------------------
- Model weights and versioned model artifact manifest (SHA256 checksums).
- Runtime container images (OCI image tarballs) with digest and provenance metadata.
- Configuration snapshots: serving configs, autoscale policies, and quantization profile used at time of snapshot.
- Tenant metadata and routing maps (redacted of PII unless contractually required).
- KV-cache snapshot (if customer requires stateful continuity) with size and TTL metadata.
- Evidence bundle (see next section) for the same window as artifacts.
- Release manifest: human-readable checklist and signatures for custody verification.

Evidence bundle specification
----------------------------
- Time window: default last 7 days, configurable per contract (minimum 72 hours).
- Included items: audit logs (admin API actions), operator runbook traces, orchestration events, health checks, and sampled request/response traces (redacted to remove customer-sensitive payloads unless authorized).
- Formats: compressed JSONL logs + accompanying index file (CSV) for quick lookup.
- Cryptographic sealing: each evidence bundle must be signed using Redwoods' signing key and include notarization by the escrow agent upon deposit.

Packaging, encryption, and key handling
--------------------------------------
- All escrow packages must be encrypted at-rest with a customer-scoped envelope key. Recommended AES-256-GCM for package encryption.
- Key escrow: two approaches supported:
  - Customer-managed KMS: Customer supplies a key ARN/identifier; Redwood encrypts package with a data key and wraps it with the customer-managed key.
  - Redwood-managed dual-control HSM: Redwood generates the key, stores wrapped copies in a dual-control HSM, and deposits a sealed copy with the escrow agent.
- Key rotation: every 90 days or per customer contract; rotation events must generate a fresh escrow deposit and updated release manifest.

Verification and periodic audits
-------------------------------
- Test deposits: Quarterly test deposit and verification with the escrow agent is required for all production Private deployments. Test includes: checksum verification, signature validation, and a simulated activation drill (without actual release).
- Annual audit: An auditor (customer or independent) may perform a full restore drill on a sandbox environment. Redwood will provide a sanitized restore kit and operator guide.
- Alerting: failures in deposit, notarization, or verification trigger P1 alerting to SRE and the assigned Customer Success Manager.

Activation & release process (high-level)
----------------------------------------
1. Activation request submitted by authorized signatories (customer legal + Redwood account lead) to escrow agent per contract.
2. Escrow agent validates trigger conditions and notifies Redwood on acceptance.
3. Redwood prepares a final sealed escrow package and transmits via agreed channel (SFTP with mutual TLS, or physical media for air-gapped) to escrow agent.
4. Escrow agent releases materials to customer or designated recovery operator after multi-party verification and identity proofing.
5. Post-release: Redwood and customer execute a joint forensic validation within 72 hours and document any gaps.

Operational runbook: activation checklist (operator-facing)
--------------------------------------------------------
1. Confirm Activation Event: validate contract clause and authorized signatories.
2. Freeze writes (if possible): coordinate with customer to quiesce tenant traffic or snapshot state.
3. Generate escrow package: run `rdi-escrow create --tenant-id <TENANT> --window 72h --out /tmp/escrow.tgz` (example CLI).
4. Compute and record checksums: `sha256sum /tmp/escrow.tgz > /tmp/escrow.sha256`.
5. Encrypt package according to customer policy; upload to escrow agent endpoint.
6. Notify SRE, Customer Success, and Legal with manifest and notarization receipt.

Acceptance criteria and conformance matrix
-----------------------------------------
| Requirement ID | Description | Default Target | Evidence Required |
| REQ-ESC-01 | Escrow deposit cadence | Daily for RPO=1h, Weekly for RPO=24h | Deposit receipts + checksums |
| REQ-EVB-02 | Evidence bundle retention | 7 days | Signed index + notarization |
| REQ-KEYS-03 | Key custody model | Dual-control HSM or Customer KMS | KMS ARN or HSM attestation |
| REQ-DR-04 | Restore verification cadence | Quarterly test deposit | Test report + corrective actions |

Legal & contract checklist (minimum clauses)
--------------------------------------------
- Activation event definition and proofing process.
- Escrow agent identity and dispute resolution.
- Data classification and redaction responsibilities.
- Liability limits and indemnities for escrowed materials.
- Timeline and SLA for release and joint validation.

Air-gapped / on-prem special considerations
-----------------------------------------
- Physical media chain-of-custody: use tamper-evident sealed media with serial numbers logged in the release manifest.
- Offline notarization: escrow agent can accept notarization receipts generated via offline signing appliances.
- Operator training: on-prem operators must complete the "Escrow and BCP field operator" curriculum before being authorized for activation procedures.

Roles and ownership
-------------------
- Solutions Engineering: define escrow scope in the order form and capture RPO/RTO in SOW.
- Customer Success: owns quarterly test scheduling and customer communication.
- SRE/Field Ops: implements deposits, encryption, and verification automation.
- Legal: negotiates escrow clauses and signatory lists.
- Procurement: selects and validates escrow agent vendors.

Templates and artifacts (location)
--------------------------------
- Sample Escrow Release Manifest: /repos/infra/docs/escrow-release-manifest-template.md
- CLI tools & runbook scripts: /repos/infra/tools/escrow (internal)
- Operator training module: Training -> Escrow and BCP (internal LMS)

Runbooks and drills
------------------
- Quarterly drill: owner (Customer Success) schedules test; SRE executes deposit and verification; legal confirms notarization.
- Post-incident activation drill: within 7 days of any P0 incident that involved service inability; full forensic evidence bundle must be preserved and deposited.

Appendix: example release manifest (human readable)
------------------------------------------------
Release manifest (excerpt)
- Tenant: example-corp
- Snapshot time: 2026-06-01T02:00:00Z
- Artifacts: models/v2.3.1.tar.gz (sha256: <hash>), runtime-images/runtime-2026-05-31.tar.gz
- Evidence bundle: evidence-2026-06-01-72h.jsonl.gz
- Encryption: AES-256-GCM, wrapped with customer-kms arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789:key/abcd-1234
- Signed-by: avery.chen@redwood.com (signature id sig-20260615)
